claim: The delta-rule update can store and replace values exactly.
label: supported
note: It matched the CPU tests with one-hot keys and gates fixed at 0 or 1. The memory demo shows why those settings matter.

claim: Neural layers can run a rule table and a small stack exactly.
label: supported
note: The lookup circuits and the stack matched the reference on the tested workloads.

claim: A learned controller does better through a typed internal interface than through a text tool.
label: supported
note: The gap was clearest on longer lists and unseen slot-value pairs, on one model and one task.

claim: Replacing integer memory with neural memory changes the answers.
label: no effect
note: With the same controller, both versions gave identical answers.

claim: Sending feedback through the model helps more than adding a trained input alone.
label: mostly refuted
note: Feedback through the model led only on the longest lists tested.

claim: Tensor implementations of dataflow, graph, and logic machines are faster than conventional code.
label: refuted
note: Plain Python led on single dataflow inputs and sparse graphs. The tensor SAT checker was faster than Python, but its search still solved fewer puzzles than WalkSAT.

claim: The machines keep their exactness in bfloat16.
label: fails past limits
note: Bit-based machines held up. Some larger integers rounded, and the filters and optimizer lost precision.

claim: An optimizer step can overwrite a value exactly.
label: one setting
note: Sequential SGD with one-hot keys and a learning rate of 1 matched in float32 and float64. The other tested settings changed what was stored.

claim: The model reads long lists better when it sees one statement at a time.
label: on this task
note: With the notebook keeping the values, it made no errors on the lists tested. Each statement could be read on its own.

claim: Putting memory inside the model helps it choose better commands.
label: proposed
note: Compare with E03 while keeping the number of trained parameters the same.

claim: A controller can learn to use the machine without seeing the right commands.
label: proposed
note: The proposed test sends a training signal from the answer back through the machine.
